cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Algorithm 5.1: Bubble Sort, steps in order.
cards.back:
Step 1: SET i = 0
Step 2: WHILE i< n REPEAT STEPS 3 to 8
Step 3: SET j = 0
Step 4: WHILE j< n-i-1,REPEAT STEPS 5 to 7
Step 5: IF numList[j] > numList[j+1] THEN
Step 6: swap(numList[j],numList[j+1])
Step 7: SET j=j+1
Step 8: SET i=i+1
cards.quote: Step 1: SET i = 0 Step 2: WHILE i< n REPEAT STEPS 3 to 8 Step 3: SET j = 0 Step 4: WHILE j< n-i-1,REPEAT STEPS 5 to 7 Step 5: IF numList[j] > numList[j+1] THEN Step 6: swap(numList[j],numList[j+1]) Step 7: SET j=j+1 Step 8: SET i=i+1
reasons: review:Pseudocode recited line by line is not a memory item; CUET tests tracing passes and outcomes, not reciting the algorithm.

cards.front: Algorithm 5.2: Selection Sort, steps in order.

Step 2: WHILE i< n REPEAT STEPS 3 to 11

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is bus topology?
cards.back: In bus topology, each communicating device connects to a common central transmission medium, known as bus.
cards.quote: In bus topology, each communicating device connects to a common central transmission medium, known as bus.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Both ring and bus topologies are considered to be ____ and ____.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is star topology?
cards.back: In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central node, which is a networking device like a hub or a switch, through separate cables.
cards.quote: In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central node, which is a networking device like a hub or a switch, through separate cables.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is tree or hybrid topology?
cards.back: It is a hierarchical topology, in which there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus.
cards.quote: It is a hierarchical topology, in which there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name teamwork components (A) to (D) of NCERT section 7.3.1, in order.
cards.back:
Communicate with Others
Listen to Others
Share with Others
Respect for Others
cards.quote: (A) Communicate with Others When a group of individuals perform one job, it is necessary to have effective communication between the members of the team. Such communication can be done via e-mails, telephones, or by arranging group meetings. This helps the team members to understand each other and sort out their problems to achieve the goal effectively. (B) Listen to Others It is necessary to understand the ideas of others while executing a job together. This can be achieved when the team members listen to each other in group meetings, and follow steps that are agreed upon. (C) Share with Others Ideas, images and tools need to be shared with each other in order to perform a job. Sharing is an important component of teamwork. Any member of the team who is well versed in a certain area should share the expertise and experience with others to effectively achieve the goal within the time frame. (D) Respect for Others
reasons: review:Front depends on letters (A) to (D) the student cannot see; the six components are one NCERT list, and a split into A-D / E-F is not recallable from the front alone. Better as one six-item card.
